title: Chilaquiles Red Salsa

description: Chilaquiles Red Salsa is a vibrant and comforting Mexican breakfast dish that transforms humble ingredients into a spectacular meal. Crispy fried tortilla chips are bathed in a rich, spicy red salsa, creating a perfect harmony of textures and flavors. It's a true taste of Mexico, often garnished with fresh cheese, cream, and onion.

fried or scrambled, optional for serving

instructions.title: Prepare Chiles and Aromatics
instructions.text: In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the dried chiles de árbol for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn them. Remove and set aside. In the same skillet, add the Roma tomatoes, garlic cloves, and white onion quarter. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until slightly charred and softened.

instructions.title: Blend the Red Salsa Base
instructions.text: Transfer the toasted chiles, charred tomatoes, garlic, and onion to a blender. Add the chicken broth. Blend until the mixture is completely smooth. For an extra fine salsa, you can strain it through a fine-mesh sieve, but it's optional for a rustic texture.

instructions.title: Cook the Salsa to Perfection
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Carefully pour the blended salsa mixture into the hot oil. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Let the salsa cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens and deepens in color. Season with salt to taste.

instructions.title: Prepare Your Tortilla Chips
instructions.text: If you're using store-bought chips, ensure they are sturdy enough to hold up to the salsa without becoming too soggy too quickly. If making your own, cut corn tortillas into triangles and fry them in hot vegetable oil until golden and crispy. Drain excess oil on paper towels and season lightly with salt.

instructions.title: Combine Chips and Salsa
instructions.text: Once the salsa has thickened, gently add the tortilla chips to the simmering red salsa. Stir carefully with a spatula or spoon to coat all the chips evenly. Cook for just 1-2 minutes, allowing the chips to soften slightly but still retain some of their texture. Do not overcook, or they will become mushy.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish Immediately
instructions.text: Immediately transfer the chilaquiles to individual serving plates. Garnish generously with crumbled queso fresco, a drizzle of crema Mexicana, finely diced red onion, and fresh cilantro. For a heartier meal, top with a freshly fried or scrambled egg. Serve hot and enjoy!

tips: For a deeper flavor, use chicken broth instead of water when blending the salsa. You can also add a pinch of cumin to the salsa for an earthy note.
Adjust the spice level by increasing or decreasing the number of chiles de árbol. For a milder salsa, remove all seeds from the chiles. For more heat, leave some in or add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
Serve chilaquiles immediately after assembling to enjoy the perfect balance of soft and slightly crispy tortilla chips. Leftovers tend to get very soggy, though they can still be delicious.
